SEMFit S7 Class

Source: R/classes.R
SEMFit.Rd

S7 class holding a structural equation model fitted by the native maximum-likelihood engine (see fit_sem()): estimates, their covariance, the parameter table, defined parameters (:=) with delta-method standard errors, and the diagnostics of the optimizer.

Usage

SEMFit(theta, vcov, table, defined, f, n_obs, n_dropped, df, information,
  converged, data, model, diagnostics, internals, call)

Arguments

theta

Named numeric vector: free-parameter estimates

vcov

Numeric matrix: covariance of theta (projected onto the active constraints and bounds; NA when the model is not identified)

table

Data frame: one row per parameter-table row with lhs, op, rhs, label, free, est and se

defined

Data frame of := parameters: name, expr, est, se

f

Numeric scalar: minimized maximum-likelihood discrepancy

n_obs, n_dropped

Integer scalars: rows used and rows dropped for missing values (listwise deletion)

df

Numeric scalar: degrees of freedom

information

Character scalar: "observed" or "expected"

converged

Logical scalar: the acceptance gate passed. fit_sem() returns a fit only for an accepted solution (otherwise it errors), so this is TRUE for every fit it returns and glance() does not report it

data

Data frame: the rows used, on the model's observed variables

model

Character scalar: the model syntax

diagnostics

List: optimizer diagnostics (status, decrement, retries, active_bounds, active_constraints, improper, sign_check, and optimum: a list with n_starts, n_accepted, best_of, certified, spread (discrepancy range among accepted starts, NA when fewer than two or not best-of), and status (unique, certified, agreed, disagreed, or single))

internals

List: the internal index objects the engine needs (ram, par_map, constraints); not part of the interface

call

Call object or NULL: the call that produced the fit

Value

A SEMFit S7 object

See also

fit_sem()

Examples

# \donttest{
fit <- fit_sem(
  "mediator1 ~ a*treatment\noutcome ~ b*mediator1 + treatment\nab := a*b",
  data = mediation_demo
)
fit@table[fit@table$op == "~", c("lhs", "rhs", "est", "se")]
#>         lhs       rhs        est         se
#> 1 mediator1 treatment 0.45599612 0.10763360
#> 2   outcome mediator1 0.71342873 0.05047202
#> 3   outcome treatment 0.04057666 0.11106057
fit@defined
#>   name expr       est         se
#> 1   ab  a*b 0.3253207 0.08016376
fit@converged
#> [1] TRUE
# }
